subject: Model shortlist, context depth and token plan for NexBridge onboarding
raw_messages:
From: Claire Reed <claire.reed@nexbridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2023 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial model & token questions for onboarding

Hi Mina / Monica,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Our engineering team dug into usage patterns and we want to lock down a short list of model candidates plus a conservative token estimate for our first 90 days. Key constraints: customer chat transcripts average ~700 tokens, many requests include a 2–3 turn convo for context, and we expect 15k unique users with ~0.05 calls/user/day initially (pilot).

Questions:
- Which model variants would you recommend for a conservative launch vs. cost-optimized steady state?
- What's the expected tokens-per-request range if we keep a 2.5-turn window and 1.2k max context?
- Can you provide a simple CSV with day-1 / week-4 / month-3 token bands so we can budget?

Attaching a shortlist template would help.

Claire
Lead, Product Integrations
NexBridge

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Reed <claire.reed@nexbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2023 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial model & token questions for onboarding

Hi Claire — thanks for the details, this is very helpful. I put together a short, opinionated starting point and a conservative token estimate CSV (attached). High level:

Model shortlist (starter -> steady):
- rdx-7b-optim (conservative low-latency / cost) — good for short responses and high throughput.
- rdx-13b-fp16 (balanced quality / latency) — recommended if you prioritize answer quality for longer spans.
- open-70b-quant (fallback / high-completion quality) — use for rare long-context jobs or when precision is mission-critical.

Context guidance:
- Suggested operating window: 1.2k tokens active context (prompt + history).
- For a 2.5-turn average, expect ~850 tokens of prompt + ~350 tokens of generated content across the turn (varies by feature).

Token bands (attached CSV):
- Day 1 conservative: 60k tokens/day (pilot traffic + safety margin)
- Week 4 scale: 250k tokens/day (ramp + feature tests)
- Month 3 steady: 1.1M tokens/day (projected 15k users at target usage pattern)

Notes on routing and cost controls:
- Start with rdx-7b-optim as default route; auto-fallback to rdx-13b for requests flagged with longer context or higher confidence needs.
- Enable prefix (KV) caching on repetitive system prompts — this removes ~10–15% of prompt tokens in our benchmarks for chat templates.

I've attached: nexbridge_model_shortlist.xlsx (shortlist + perf notes) and token_estimates_q2.csv (bands). Happy to sync and walk through the numbers.

—Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nexbridge_model_shortlist.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)
Attachment: token_estimates_q2.csv (csv, 8KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2023 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: NexBridge notes & burst scenarios

Mina / Marissa — quick internal note before we jump on the call with Claire tomorrow.

Highlights from Mina's reply: rdx-7b default + rdx-13b for quality sensitive calls. Token bands look reasonable, but I want to flag two operational items to confirm with eng:

1) Burst tolerance: NexBridge expects occasional support spikes (estimate: 3x baseline for 1–2 hours during business opens). Recommend we provision burst-friendly autoscaling with a cap to avoid runaway spend.

2) Canary & model pins: For first two weeks use pinned rdx-7b per endpoint, allow manual switch to rdx-13b for A/B test cohorts. We should surface a rollback playbook in the kickoff doc.

Ask for the call: can we get a sample of per-hour traffic for a weekend vs weekday so I can refine the hourly token forecast? Also confirm whether transcripts include attachments or base64 content (that affects prompt sizes).

—Monica
Customer Success Manager

---

From: Claire Reed <claire.reed@nexbridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: NexBridge Eng Team <eng@nexbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 24 May 2023 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial model & token questions for onboarding

Thanks — this looks great. I reviewed the spreadsheet and the Day-1 conservative band is exactly what our finance lead requested. Two quick follow-ups:

- We'll send a sample per-hour export by EOD tomorrow so you can refine burst estimates.
- Can you include the suggested model pin/rollout steps in the kickoff agenda and a draft rollback playbook?

Let's schedule the implementation kickoff for next Tuesday; Claire + two engineers will join. Timezone: PST.

Claire Reed
Lead, Product Integrations
NexBridge
